zh: 4. 基督教的兴起
en: 4. The Rise of Christianity

zh: 日趋黑暗的时代
en: THE DARKENING AGE

zh: 基督教的兴起是历史上最非凡的现象之一。它发生在与奴隶社会解体相关的动荡与变革时期，这种动荡与变革在旧的道德、哲学和宗教的危机中得到了体现。处于衰落阶段的罗马帝国，为神秘主义思想的传播提供了肥沃的土壤。这在一定程度上解释了来自东方的新宗教为何能迅速传播。旧的宗教和道德体系所代表的世界已经过时，即将成为历史。
en: The rise of Christianity is one of the most extraordinary phenomena in history. It occurred at a time of upheaval and change associated with the dissolution of slave society, which found its reflection in a crisis of the old morality, philosophy and religion. The Roman Empire in the phase of its decline was a fertile ground for the spread of mystical ideas. This partly explains the rapid spread of new religions from the East. The old religion and morality represented a world that had outlived its usefulness and was already on the point of passing into history.

zh: 神庙空无一人，人们寻求一种能为他们无尽的苦难提供些许慰藉、并带来救赎希望的宗教。在此背景下，“救世主”、“救赎者”的理念具有显而易见的吸引力。要通过革命推翻奴隶制，唯一的真正希望本应是让奴隶与罗马无产阶级——即罗马那些没有财产的自由公民大众——联合起来。但罗马无产阶级与现代工人阶级不同，是一个非生产性的、寄生于国家的阶级。真正的生产阶级是奴隶，整个压迫体系正是建立在他们的背上。
en: The temples stood empty and people sought a religion that would offer them some consolation for their endless suffering, and some prospect of salvation. In this context, the idea of a Saviour, a Redeemer, had an obvious attraction. The only real hope for a revolutionary overthrow of slavery would have been to unite the slaves with the Roman proletariat – the mass of propertyless, free citizens in Rome. But the Roman proletariat, unlike the modern working class, was a non-productive, parasitic class that lived off the state. The real productive class was the slaves, on whose backs the whole oppressive edifice rested.

zh: 在《路易·波拿巴的雾月十八日》中，卡尔·马克思引用了西斯蒙迪的论断：“罗马无产阶级靠社会养活，而现代社会则靠无产阶级养活。”
从心理特征来看，罗马无产阶级与美国内战时期南方各州的贫困白人颇为相似。尽管他们是社会最底层的人，被富有的奴隶主蔑称为“白人垃圾”，但归根结底，他们却站在奴隶主一边，反对奴隶。因此，尽管在伟大的革命领袖斯巴达克斯的领导下取得过一些辉煌的胜利，但作为罗马共和国晚期标志的众多奴隶起义，最终还是不可避免地以失败告终。
en: In The Eighteenth Brumaire, Karl Marx quoted Sismondi’s statement: “The Roman proletariat lived at the expense of society, while modern society lives at the expense of the proletariat.”

In its psychology, the Roman proletariat resembled the poor whites of the southern states of the USA at the time of the Civil War. Although they were the lowest of the low, regarded contemptuously by the wealthy slave owners as ‘white trash’, in the last analysis, they sided with the slave owners against the slaves. As a result, the numerous slave uprisings that characterised the late Roman Republic, despite some spectacular victories under the great revolutionary leader Spartacus, inevitably ended in defeat.

zh: 早期基督徒
en: THE EARLY CHRISTIANS

zh: 早期基督徒构成了一个以社会中的贫穷和受压迫阶层为基础的革命运动。早期基督教的阶级性质在《福音书》中得到了如实反映。《使徒行传》表明，早期基督徒信奉平等。信徒们的团契以原始共产主义的形式体现出来。
en: The early Christians were a revolutionary movement based on the poor and oppressed layers of society. The class nature of early Christianity is faithfully reflected in the gospels. The Acts of the Apostles show that the early Christians believed in equality. The communion of believers was expressed in the form of primitive communism.

zh: 所有加入这一团契的人，首先必须放弃他们所有的世俗财产。德尔图良（约公元155—220 年）写道：
en: All who joined this communion had first to relinquish all their worldly goods. Tertullian (c. 155-220 AD) wrote:

zh: ……我们的兄弟情谊是由家庭财产维系的，而这种财产在你们中间通常会瓦解兄弟情谊。因此，我们这些在思想和灵魂上团结一致的人，毫不犹豫地分享财产。在我们中间，一切都是共有的——除了我们的妻子。在这一点上，我们终止了共有，而这恰恰是其他人实行共有的唯一领域。
en: … our brotherhood is upheld by the family substance, which among you as a rule dissolves the fraternal tie. So we, who are united in mind and soul, have no hesitation about sharing property. All is common among us – except our wives. At that point we dissolve our partnership, which is the one place where the rest of men make it effective.

zh: 约翰·阿莱格罗指出：
en: John Allegro notes:

zh: 早期教会也实行了一种形式的共产主义，与以耶路撒冷教派为代表的犹太教正统势力针锋相对，举行某种形式的仪式性餐宴，为入教者施洗，并特别重视圣经先知们的教导——人们认为先知们的每一句话都能为人类的未来提供洞见。
en: The early Church also observed a form of communism, was at loggerheads with established Jewry as represented by the Jerusalem cultus, practised a ritual meal of some kind, baptised its initiates, and paid special regard to the teachings of the biblical prophets, whose every word was thought to offer insight into the future of mankind.

zh: 早期基督徒深信，社会的深刻危机预示着世界末日的临近、基督的再临以及新耶路撒冷的降临。对他们而言，这并非云端之国，而是在地上真实存在的上帝之国。他们致力于与现存秩序进行不懈的斗争——《启示录》（现存基督教文献中最早且最真实的一部）将现存秩序描述为“巴比伦大淫妇”。他们秉持着一种自豪而顽强的革命立场。
en: The early Christians were convinced that the profound crisis of society heralded the imminent end of the world, the second coming of Christ and the emergence of the New Jerusalem. For them this was not a kingdom in the clouds, but a very real kingdom of God on earth. They were committed to an unrelenting struggle against the existing order, which the Book of Revelation – the earliest and most authentic of surviving Christian texts – describes as the ‘Whore of Babylon’. They adopted a proud and obstinate revolutionary standpoint.

zh: 面对异教法官，他们依然顽强坚定，拒绝放弃信仰，甘愿接受殉道，并对最终的胜利充满信心。他们迫切地期待着基督的即将来临和千年王国的降临，相信那即将破晓。最初，基督教是一个犹太教派。正是保罗提出了使非犹太人皈依的主张，废除了割礼和饮食禁令——这些曾是争取非犹太人皈依的严重障碍。这一举措被证明极为成功。
en: They remained stubbornly steadfast before the heathen judges, refusing to renounce their faith and willingly embracing martyrdom, confident in their final victory. They impatiently awaited the imminent return of Christ and the thousand-year kingdom, which was shortly to dawn. Originally, Christianity had been a Jewish sect. It was Paul who developed the idea of converting non-Jews, eliminating circumcision and the dietary prohibitions that were serious obstacles to winning over the latter. It proved to be extremely successful.

zh: 弗里德里希·恩格斯解释道：
en: Friedrich Engels explained:

zh: 最早的基督徒是从什么样的人群中招募而来的？主要是来自“劳苦和受压迫者”，即社会最底层的成员，这正符合革命力量的特征。而他们又由哪些人组成呢？在城镇里，是贫困的自由民——形形色色的人，比如南方奴隶州的“卑微的白人”，以及殖民地和中国海港里的欧洲流浪汉和冒险家；还有获释的奴隶，尤其是奴隶；在意大利、西西里和非洲的大型庄园里，有奴隶；而在各省的农村地区，则有因债务而日益陷入奴役状态的小农。对于所有这些人来说，根本不存在一条通向解放的共同道路。对他们所有人而言，天堂都已沦为身后的往事；对那些破产的自由人来说，那是昔日的城邦——既是城镇，也是国家——他们的祖先曾是那里的自由公民；对战俘奴隶来说，那是他们被征服和囚禁前的自由时光；对小农来说，则是已被废除的氏族社会制度和公社土地所有制。这一切都被征服者罗马那只抹平一切的铁拳摧毁了……

在纯粹或以自然经济为主的地区，税收的压力及其引发的货币需求，使农民陷入对高利贷者日益加深的束缚之中，导致贫富差距巨大，富者愈富，穷者则彻底赤贫。孤立的小部落或城镇对庞大的罗马世界强权所作的任何抵抗都毫无希望。对于那些被奴役、受压迫和贫困的人们来说，出路和救赎在哪里？对于这些利益互不相通甚至相互对立的各异群体而言，又何处存在一条共同的出路？然而，若要让一场伟大的革命运动将他们全部囊括其中，就必须找到这条出路。

这一出路被找到了。但并非在现世。就当时的情况而言，它只能是一种宗教层面的出路。于是，一个新世界被接纳了。肉体死亡后灵魂的永生，已逐渐成为整个罗马世界公认的信仰条目。对亡者灵魂在世时所作所为予以某种报偿或惩罚的观念，也获得了越来越广泛的认可。就报偿而言，诚然，前景并不乐观：古代社会那样朴素的唯物主义倾向，使其必然将尘世生活视为比阴间生活具有无限更大的价值；对希腊人而言，死后继续存在反而被视为一种不幸。随后基督教兴起，它严肃对待来世的奖赏与惩罚，创造了天堂与地狱，并找到了一条出路，将那些劳苦负重的人们从这充满悲痛的尘世引向永恒的乐园。事实上，只有凭借来世奖赏的希望，斯多葛派和斐洛派所倡导的超脱尘世与苦行主义，才能被提升为一种新的世界性宗教的基本道德原则，从而激发受压迫的大众的热情。
en: What kind of people were the first Christians recruited from? Mainly from the ‘labouring and burdened’, the members of the lowest strata, as becomes a revolutionary element. And what did they consist of? In the towns of impoverished free men, all sorts of people, like the ‘mean whites’ of the southern slave states and the European beachcombers and adventurers in colonial and Chinese seaports, then of freedmen and, above all, slaves; on the large estates in Italy, Sicily, and Africa of slaves, and in the rural districts of the provinces of small peasants who had fallen more and more into bondage through debt. There was absolutely no common road to emancipation for all these elements. For all of them paradise lay lost behind them; for the ruined free men it was the former polis, the town and the state at the same time, of which their forefathers had been free citizens; for the war-captive slaves the time of freedom before their subjugation and captivity; for the small peasants the abolished gentile social system and communal landownership. All that had been smitten down by the levelling iron fist of conquering Rome…

The pressure of taxation and the need for money which it caused in regions with a purely or predominant natural economy plunged the peasants into ever deeper bondage to the usurers, gave rise to great differences in fortune, making the rich richer and the poor completely destitute. Any resistance by isolated small tribes or towns to the gigantic Roman world power was without prospect. Where was the way out, salvation, for the enslaved, oppressed and impoverished, a way out common to all these diverse groups of people whose interests were mutually alien or even opposed? And yet it had to be found if a great revolutionary movement was to embrace them all.

This way out was found. But not in this world. As things were, it could only be a religious way out. Then a new world was embraced. The continued life of the soul after the death of the body had gradually become a recognised article of faith through-out the Roman world. A kind of recompense or punishment of the deceased souls for their actions while on earth also received more and more general recognition. As far as recompense was concerned, admittedly, the prospects were not so good: antiquity was too primitively materialistic not to attribute infinitely greater value to life on earth than to life in the shades; to live on after death was considered by the Greeks rather as a misfortune. Then came Christianity, which took seriously recompense and punishment in the world beyond and created heaven and hell, and a way out was found which would lead the labouring and burdened from this vale of woe to eternal paradise. And in fact only with the prospect of a reward in the world beyond could the stoico-philonic renunciation of the world and ascetics be exalted to the basic moral principle of a new world religion which would enthuse the oppressed masses.

zh: 教会具有显而易见的吸引力：在一个动荡不安、充满焦虑的时代，它为每个人提供了得救的希望和死后生命的承诺。相比之下，旧神显得冷漠而疏远。但当新宗教脱离其最初的犹太语境时，它便被扭曲、改变得面目全非，变成了截然不同的东西。这导致了新的矛盾。尽管新宗教最初最狂热的信徒来自社会中最受压迫和边缘化的群体（奴隶和妇女），但它逐渐吸引了一批受过教育且享有特权的阶层的关注——这些人因衰败社会中的精神空虚而日益感到疏离。随着时间的推移，早期教会调整并规范了其教义，以适应其在社会中的新地位。
en: The Church had an obvious appeal: in a troubled and anxious age, it offered every individual the hope of salvation and the promise of life after death. By contrast, the old gods seemed cold and aloof. But when the new religion broke out of its original Jewish context, it was mangled, changed beyond recognition and turned into something quite different. This led to new contradictions. Although the new religion found its first and most enthusiastic adepts in the most oppressed and marginalised elements of society (slaves and women), it gradually attracted the attention of a layer of the educated and privileged classes, who were increasingly alienated by the spiritual emptiness of a decadent society. Over a period, the early Church changed and regulated its doctrines to suit its new position in society.

zh: 国家镇压试图扼杀基督教运动的所有努力均告失败。尽管遭受了最残酷的迫害，基督徒仍赢得了大众的支持。因此，统治阶级采取了他们在这种情况下惯常的做法。如果无法用武力击败一场运动，压迫阶级就会诉诸诡计。他们收买领袖。那个无原则的玩世不恭者君士坦丁（公元306—337 年）意识到，基督教无法通过镇压被扼杀，于是决定，最佳策略是通过贿赂其领袖——主教们——并将其收编，从而消解这一运动的反抗力量。
en: All the attempts to crush the Christian movement by state repression failed. Despite the most ferocious persecution, the Christians won mass support. Therefore, the ruling class did what they always do in such circumstances. If they cannot defeat a movement by force, the oppressor classes resort to cunning. They corrupt the leaders. The unprincipled cynic Constantine (306-337 AD) realised that the Christians could not be crushed by repression and decided that the best tactic was to neuter them by bribing their leaders, the bishops, and co-opting them.

zh: 在公元100 至300 年左右的时期，我们看到主教们的权力逐渐巩固，一个享有特权的官僚阶层逐渐形成。基督教教会逐渐建立起一套官僚机构，并与罗马国家融为一体。
en: In the period of approximately 100-300 AD we see a gradual consolidation of the power of the bishops, the crystallisation of a privileged bureaucratic stratum. Gradually, the Christian Church acquired a bureaucratic apparatus, which fused with the Roman state.

zh: 主教们最初是司库。他们开始将大量财富和权力集中于自己手中。英国历史学家爱德华·吉本在其鸿篇巨著《罗马帝国衰亡史》中，在一则尖锐的脚注中写道：
en: The bishops were originally the treasurers. They began to concentrate considerable wealth and authority in their hands. In a biting footnote, the English historian Edward Gibbon, in his monumental work The Decline and Fall of the Roman Empire, writes:

zh: 我曾在某处听闻或读到一位本笃会修道院院长的坦率自白：“我的贫穷誓言使我每年获得十万克朗；我的服从誓言则使我升至君主之位。”
en: I have somewhere heard or read the frank confession of a Benedictine abbot: “My vow of poverty has given me an hundred thousand crowns a year; my vow of obedience has raised me to the rank of a sovereign prince.”

zh: 吉本以其一贯的讽刺口吻，不禁好奇这位修道院院长的贞洁誓言究竟会将他引向何等放纵的行为。
en: With his characteristic irony, Gibbon wonders to what excesses the abbot’s vows of chastity had led him.

zh: 君士坦丁
en: CONSTANTINE

zh: 当新宗教最终被君士坦丁皇帝承认后，它便转变为与其截然相反的存在。教会从一个由穷人和受压迫者组成的革命运动，被国家所吸收，进而成为富人和权贵手中的一件强大武器。君士坦丁准确地算计到，放弃旧宗教可能带来的任何不利影响，都将被拥有教会这一盟友所带来的好处所抵消——教会拥有强大的组织体系，并能控制大众。
en: When the new religion was eventually recognised by the Emperor Constantine, it changed into its opposite. From being a revolutionary movement of the poor and oppressed, the Church was absorbed into the state to become a formidable weapon in the hands of the rich and powerful. Constantine calculated correctly that any disadvantages that might flow from the abandonment of the old religion would be outweighed by the advantages of having the Church, with its powerful apparatus and control over the masses, as an ally.

zh: 这位机会主义者利用宗教来巩固自己的权力。基督教早期教义带有强烈的革命和共产主义色彩，一旦基督教被接纳为国教，这些教义便被作为异端加以迫害并彻底铲除。为此，教会必须作为帝国国家的一部分实现中央集权。结果，罗马主教——原本并无特殊地位（且本应隶属于耶路撒冷主教）——如今被提升为教会的最高领袖——教皇。
en: This opportunist used religion to strengthen his grip on power. The earlier doctrines of the Christians, with their strong revolutionary and communist overtones, were persecuted as heresy and stamped out once Christianity became accepted as the state religion. To do this the Church had to be centralised as part of the imperial state. As a result, the bishop of Rome, who originally had no special status (and would have been subordinate to the bishop of Jerusalem), was now elevated to the Supreme Head of the Church – the Pope.

zh: 正是君士坦丁在耶路撒冷建造了圣墓教堂及其他“圣地”，尽管声称这些地方就是传说中的圣地，实际上毫无依据。据说君士坦丁的母亲海伦娜是某位鱼贩的女儿，她曾前往耶路撒冷，试图获取据称用于钉死基督的钉子、原始十字架的木片，甚至还有他母亲乳房里流出的乳汁！
en: It was Constantine who built the church of the Holy Sepulchre and other ‘Holy Places’ in Jerusalem, although there was absolutely no basis for claiming that these places were what they were supposed to be. Constantine’s mother, Helena, who is said to have been the daughter of a fishmonger, went to Jerusalem to obtain the nails that were supposed to have been used in the crucifixion of Christ, together with pieces of wood from the original cross, and even some milk from his mother’s breasts!

zh: 天主教会至今仍掌控着这些“圣地”，每年从中获利颇丰。教会及其统治精英开始积累巨额财富。事实上，推行独身制其实是一项旨在保护教会财产、防止其通过继承流向子女的措施。
en: The Catholic Church still has possession of these ‘Holy Places’, which every year bring in a handsome profit. The Church and its ruling elite began to amass vast amounts of wealth. In fact, the introduction of the rule of celibacy was actually a measure to protect Church property and prevent it being lost to children through inheritance.

zh: 正统
en: ORTHODOXY

zh: 在公元二世纪的前几十年里，存在着大量相互对立的基督教派，各派都有自己的福音书和礼仪，彼此之间冲突激烈。这造成了一个问题。必须只有一位皇帝、一个国家、一种宗教、一位神和一个教会。若否认其中任何一项，就必须否定所有这些。为了巩固自己的权力，君士坦丁不得不铲除基督教内部所有相互竞争的派别，并确立正统教义。铲除这些“异端”经历了一系列血腥战争。君士坦丁通过国家暴力强行建立秩序，同时借助教会当局所施加的“永恒惩罚”这一更严峻的威胁——此时的教会已沦为国家权力的附庸。
en: In the first decades of the second century there were a large number of rival Christian sects, each with their own gospels and rites, that were in bitter conflict. This presented a problem. There had to be one emperor, one state, one religion, one god and one Church. Deny one of these things and you must deny them all. In order to consolidate his power, Constantine had to eliminate all competing versions of Christianity and introduce orthodoxy. It took a series of bloody wars to extirpate these ‘heresies’. Constantine imposed order by state violence, backed up by the even greater threat of eternal punishment wielded by the authorities of a Church that had become merely an arm of the state power.

zh: 经文被反复清洗，以抹去早期基督教原始革命和共产主义信息的任何痕迹，如今流传的《新约》版本中仅存寥寥残迹。但要彻底清除其中的革命内容是不可能的。后来，在西欧，教会以一种非常简单的方式绕过了这一难题：《圣经》仅以拉丁文提供，而绝大多数人根本不懂拉丁文。唯一被允许解释经文的是神职人员，他们逐渐作为一种特殊的特权阶层与社会隔绝开来。
en: The scriptures were repeatedly purged to wipe out all traces of the original revolutionary and communist message of early Christianity, with only a few remnants in the version of the New Testament available today. But it was impossible to remove the revolutionary content completely. Later, in western Europe, the Church got round this difficulty very simply: the Bible was only made available in Latin, which the overwhelming majority did not understand. The only ones allowed to interpret the scriptures were the priests, who were gradually separated from society as a special privileged caste.

zh: 从一开始，福音书的权威就逐渐通过传统确立起来。福音书甚至并未声称是由基督的门徒所写，但人们逐渐接受了这一说法——这完全是传统力量使然，别无其他原因。到三世纪末，流传的福音书至少有二十部，此外还有大量书信、耶稣基督的生平传记及箴言等，总数超过八十部。这种状况令君士坦丁无法容忍，他决定一劳永逸地终结这一切。
en: From the very beginning, the authority of the gospels was gradually acquired by tradition. The gospels do not even claim to have been written by the Disciples of Christ, but gradually, people have accepted that they were – from force of tradition, and nothing else. By the end of the third century there were at least twenty gospels in circulation, as well as numerous letters, lives and sayings of Jesus Christ etc., amounting to more than eighty in total. This situation was intolerable to Constantine, who decided to put an end to it once and for all.

zh: 尼西亚大公会议
en: THE COUNCIL OF NICAEA

zh: 正是由君士坦丁组织的尼西亚大公会议（公元325 年），正式解决了所有争议问题，例如耶稣的神性。但如今鲜有人知晓这一结果是如何达成的。在比提尼亚的尼西亚城，由君士坦丁亲自监督的一支由基督教主教及其随从组成的代表团，花了许多天的时间，深入探讨了基督的本质和三位一体这一棘手问题。圣子如何同时也是圣父？圣灵又该如何理解？即使在会议结束时，这些问题仍未得到令人满意的解决。当时仍未达成一致的文本，但这对他们中的大多数人来说可能并不重要，因为他们根本不识字。
en: It was the Council of Nicaea (325 AD), organised by Constantine, that formally settled all the disputed issues, such as the divinity of Jesus. But few people nowadays are aware of the methods whereby this result was achieved. For many days, in the Bithynian city of Nicaea, a delegation of Christian bishops and their retinues, overseen by Constantine himself, pondered the problematic question of the nature of Christ and the Trinity. How could the Son be also the Father, and what about God the Holy Ghost? These questions were not satisfactorily resolved even when the Council ended. There was still no agreed text, which probably did not matter to most of them, since they could not read.

zh: 关于这次著名的会议，我们知之甚少，因为它已被教会从历史记载中抹去——教会希望掩盖当时发生的事情的真相。会议现场挤满了君士坦丁的爪牙，他们乐于执行皇帝的意志。与会的主教们是一群乌合之众：其中一些是前奴隶或前囚犯，来自印度边境、埃及、撒哈拉沙漠、波斯、英格兰、非洲、希腊等遥远而陌生的地方。许多人支持各种异端教派：阿里乌派、多纳图斯派、诺斯替派等。
en: Very little is known about this celebrated meeting because it has been erased from the historical record by the Church, who wished to hide the truth about what went on. The Council was packed by Constantine’s henchmen, who were willing to carry out the will of the emperor. The bishops were a motley crew: some were ex-slaves or ex-convicts from as far afield as the border with India, Egypt, the Sahara Desert, Persia, England, Africa, Greece and other exotic places. Many were supporters of an array of heretical sects: Arians, Donatists, Gnostics, etc.

zh: 这些人与支持君士坦丁的那些受过良好教育的阴谋家相比，根本无力在辩论中与之抗衡。当时有若干问题令皇帝深感恼火，例如基督徒拒绝服兵役或崇拜皇帝。但这些问题可以通过明智的策略加以应对。况且，所有试图通过镇压摧毁教会的尝试都已失败。皇帝的亲临本身就足以让在场者吓得双腿发抖。许多人可能从未见过他，更不用说如此近距离了。如果心理威慑还不够，还有其他更直接的方法可用。
en: Such men were in no position to compete in debate with the educated intriguers who supported Constantine. There were a number of problems that irked the Emperor such as the refusal of Christians to serve in the army or worship the Emperor. But these could be managed with intelligent tactics. And in any case, all attempts to destroy the Church through repression had failed. The presence of the emperor was in itself enough to make those present shake in their sandals. Many probably had never seen him before, and certainly not this close. And if psychological intimidation was not enough, other more direct methods were available.

zh: 在场的一些人曾奉他的命令遭受过酷刑。这些酷刑包括用烙铁挖出眼睛，或割断腿部韧带，以及其他令人“愉悦”的“劝说”手段，这些手段会让人失明或致残。这些人自然不愿重蹈覆辙。但为了确保投票结果，在会议结束前，一些代表因过于直率地表达了自己的想法，遭到了谋杀或失踪，从此杳无音讯。
en: Some of those present had already suffered torture at his command. These tortures included having an eye extracted with a hot iron, or having one’s leg ligaments cut, and other pleasant methods of persuasion that left one blind or crippled. These men would not be eager to repeat the experience. But, just to make sure of the vote, before the meeting ended, some delegates had been murdered or disappeared, never to be seen again, for having expressed their thoughts with excessive frankness.

zh: 最终，仅剩寥寥数部被认可的著作流传至今，即我们所知的《圣经》。人们能读什么、不能读什么，是由无休止的宗教战争、清洗、迫害和殉道所决定的。镇压异端的斗争漫长、残酷且血腥，持续了数百年之久。其残暴程度远超异教徒对基督教发起的任何迫害。
en: In the end, there remained a small handful of accepted works that have come down to us as the Bible. What people could or could not read was decided by an endless series of religious wars, purges, persecution and martyrdom. The struggle to suppress heresy was long, bitter and bloody, and it lasted for hundreds of years. It was far more vicious than any of the persecutions launched by the pagans against Christianity.

zh: 迫害与毁灭
en: PERSECUTION AND DESTRUCTION

zh: 对其他宗教的迫害几乎立即开始。公元386 年，一项法律通过，宣布那些“因宗教问题争论不休者……应以生命和鲜血来承担叛国罪的惩罚”。
书籍被系统性地焚毁。耶路撒冷的埃利亚·卡皮托利纳军事殖民地为建造一座基督教教堂而摧毁了一座异教神庙。这仅仅是长达数个世纪的漫长运动的开端，该运动最终导致世界各地许多辉煌文明被彻底铲除。
en: The persecution of other religions commenced almost immediately. In 386 AD, a law was passed declaring that those “who contend about religion … shall pay the penalty of high treason with their lives and blood.”

Books were systematically burned. The military colony of Aelia Capitolina in Jerusalem destroyed a pagan temple for the purpose of constructing a Christian church. This was only the beginning of a long campaign that lasted centuries and led to the wholesale eradication of many brilliant cultures in all parts of the world.

zh: 西班牙征服者在基督的旗帜下，在其美洲殖民地屠杀了数百万男女老幼。他们将无价的艺术品熔化成黄金，并在玛雅人和阿兹特克人的神庙废墟之上建造了基督教教堂和大教堂。基督徒随后在欧洲、中东、非洲、澳大利亚及其他地区摧毁了数千种古老的宗教和文化。罗马帝国晚期对异教徒的迫害始于君士坦丁统治时期。基督徒对任何稍带理性思考和哲学色彩的事物都怀有刻骨的敌意。他们不遗余力地要将旧世界连根拔起。吉本指出：
en: The Spanish Conquistadores slaughtered millions of men, women and children in their American colonies under the banners of Christ. They melted down priceless objects of art for gold and they built Christian churches and cathedrals over the ruined temples of the Mayas and Aztecs. Christians went on to destroy thousands of ancient religions and cultures in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, Australia and elsewhere. The persecution of pagans in the late Roman Empire began during the reign of Constantine. The Christians were bitterly hostile to anything remotely resembling rational thought and philosophy. They were hell-bent on tearing up the old world, root and branch. Gibbon remarks:

zh: 基督徒们——他们借助恶灵的干预，便能轻而易举地解释一切超自然现象——不仅愿意，甚至渴望接受异教神话中最离奇的虚构故事。但基督徒的信仰却伴随着恐惧。他认为，对本民族宗教崇拜所表现出的哪怕是最微不足道的敬意，都是对恶魔的直接膜拜，也是对上帝威严的叛逆行为。
en: The Christians, who, by the interposition of evil spirits, could so readily explain every præternatural appearance, were disposed and even desirous to admit the most extravagant fictions of the Pagan mythology. But the belief of the Christian was accompanied with horror. The most trifling mark of respect to the national worship he considered as a direct homage yielded to the dæmon, and as an act of rebellion against the majesty of God.

zh: 基督徒自己也公开承认了对旧宗教的这种憎恶。试看圣奥古斯丁的以下言论：“消灭异教徒和异教信众的所有迷信，正是上帝所愿、上帝所命、上帝所宣告的！”
en: This hatred of the old religions was openly admitted by the Christians themselves. Take the following words of St. Augustine: “That all superstition of pagans and heathens should be annihilated is what God wants, God commands, God proclaims!”

zh: 那是一个充满迷信的时代，人们相信通过使用魔法符号、咒语和仪式，便能召唤出超自然的力量。他们相信奇迹。为了赢得民心，教会必须提供大量奇迹。凯撒利亚的优西比乌——一位撰写了第一部君士坦丁传记的基督教圣经学者兼历史学家——将十字架描绘成一个魔法符号，其效力据称由以下故事所证实——显然，这个故事是他为了自身目的而杜撰的。
en: This was a superstitious time, when people believed it possible to conjure up supernatural powers by the use of magic signs, formulas and rites. They believed in miracles. To win popularity, the Church had to provide a plentiful supply of miracles. Eusebius of Caesarea, a Christian biblical scholar and historian who wrote the first biography of Constantine, portrayed the cross as a magical sign, the effectiveness of which was said to be proved by the following story, which he clearly invented for his own purposes.

zh: 篡位者君士坦丁于公元312 年10 月28 日取得了一场重大胜利。米尔维安桥之战是内战的最后一场战役，通过这场战役，他成为了皇帝。优西比乌声称，在战斗开始前，君士坦丁和他的军队在太阳上方的天空中看到了一道光之十字架，上面有希腊文，通常被翻译成拉丁文为“In hoc signo vinces”——“凭此标志，你必得胜”。当晚，君士坦丁做了一个梦，梦中基督告诉他，应以十字架的标志对抗敌人。随后，他下令士兵们在盾牌上绘制这个基督教符号，这自然使他取得了压倒性的胜利。
en: The usurper Constantine won a great victory on 28 October 312 AD. The Battle of the Milvian Bridge was the final battle of the civil war, by which he became Emperor. Eusebius claims that, before the battle, Constantine and his army saw a cross of light in the sky above the sun with words in Greek that are generally translated into Latin as “In hoc signo vinces” – “In this sign thou shalt conquer”. That night Constantine had a dream in which Christ told him he should use the sign of the cross against his enemies. He then ordered his soldiers to mark the Christian symbol on their shields, which naturally gave him overwhelming victory.

zh: 这个故事的真实性——就像优西比乌所写的一切一样——值得怀疑。关于这场战役的最早记载可追溯至公元313 年，其中并未提及任何异象或梦境。但无论如何，显而易见的是，这场战役的胜利并非源于十字架的标志，而是源于锋利的钢刃以及挥舞这些武器的战士们强健的臂膀。
en: The truth of this story – like everything else Eusebius writes – is open to doubt. The earliest account of the battle, dating from 313 AD, mentions nothing about a vision or a dream. But it is in any case self-evident that the battle was won, not by the sign of the cross, but by sharp steel blades and the strong arms of the men that wielded them.

zh: 公元315 年，元老院在罗马为君士坦丁竖立了一座凯旋门，其铭文赞颂他“在神明的启示下”率军取得了胜利。铭文巧妙地避开了具体是哪位神明提供了“启示”，市民们可以将其归功于“不败之太阳神”、基督教神明，或是他们选择的任何神明。实际上，没有任何历史证据表明君士坦丁曾皈依基督教。他生前从未自称是基督徒，据说他只是在临终时才皈依。但我们对此仅能依据优西比乌的说法，而他几乎在所有事情上都在说谎。早期基督教完全浸透了此类迷信。
en: In 315 AD the Senate dedicated a triumphal arch in Rome to Constantine with an inscription praising him because ‘with divine instigation’ he and his army had won the victory. It tactfully refrained from saying which god had provided the ‘instigation’ and citizens could credit it to Sol Invictus or the Christian deity or whichever god they chose. Actually, there is not a shred of historical evidence that Constantine was ever converted to Christianity. He never actually claimed to be a Christian during his lifetime and it is said that he only converted on his deathbed. But we only have Eusebius’ word for that, and he lied about practically everything. Early Christianity was thoroughly impregnated with such superstition.

zh: 教会教父们摒弃理性，宣扬盲目信仰，这可概括为据称出自德尔图良的那句名言：“Credo, quia absurdum est”——“我信，正因其荒谬”。科学被视为可疑之物，是异教的遗产。在所讨论的这一时期，异教祭司和哲学家是早期基督徒的主要攻击目标，因为他们深知这些人是异教社会和文化中的精神和知识精英。一旦消灭了他们，使异教徒皈依的任务就会变得简单得多。而他们正是这样做的。
en: In place of reason, the Church Fathers preached blind faith, summed up in the celebrated phrase attributed to Tertullian, “Credo, quia absurdum est” – “I believe because it is absurd”. Science was looked on as suspicious, a heritage of paganism. In the period under consideration, pagan priests and philosophers were the primary target of the early Christians, who knew they were the spiritual and intellectual elite of the pagan society and culture. Once they were destroyed, it would be a simpler task to convert the pagans. And this is what they did.

zh: 他们对犹太人的态度，可从一位最著名的早期教会教父——圣约翰·克里索斯托（“金口”之名由此而来）——的一段话中体现出来：“……会堂……是强盗的巢穴，是野兽的栖身之所……是恶魔的居所……”
1500年后，纳粹德国曾赞同地引用了这些话。
en: Their attitude to the Jews is shown by a statement of one of the most celebrated early Church Fathers, St. John Chrysostom – he of the Golden Mouth: “… the synagogue … is a den of robbers and a lodging for wild beasts … a dwelling of demons …”
These words were quoted with approval in Nazi Germany 1,500 years later.

zh: 今天，当我们漫步于雅典那些令人惊叹的国家博物馆，欣赏古希腊雕像那奇迹般的艺术造诣时，我们的赞叹之中却掺杂着一种深切的悲痛——因为古典希腊的艺术瑰宝已大量失传。在整个希腊，肆意破坏的痕迹随处可见：残破的神庙、失去头颅的神祇雕像，都在无声地见证着那场破坏狂欢。人们或许会认为，这种蓄意破坏文化的行径是野蛮人的所作所为。但这种推测是根本错误的。这一罪行是由基督徒在狄奥多西皇帝（公元392—395 年）的唆使下实施的。
en: Today, as we walk through the marvellous national museums of Athens, admiring the miraculous artistry of its ancient statues, our admiration is tinged with a profound sense of sorrow at the loss of so much of the art of classical Greece. All over Greece, the evidence of wanton destruction is plain to see: ruined temples, headless statues of gods and goddesses bear mute witness to an orgy of vandalism. One might suppose that this deliberate destruction of culture was the work of the barbarians. But this supposition would be fundamentally mistaken. This crime was perpetrated by Christians at the instigation of Emperor Theodosius (392-395 AD).

zh: 在此之前，罗马仍以异教徒居多，而非基督徒。在高卢、西班牙和意大利北部，除城市地区外，其余地区仍顽固地效忠于旧神。就连米兰也仍有一半人口信奉异教。但这一切即将改变。公元392 年，狄奥多西成为罗马帝国东西两部分的皇帝；他是最后一位统治帝国全境的皇帝。同年，他下令摧毁帝国各地的异教神庙。他颁布了一项全面法令，禁止进行任何形式的异教祭祀或崇拜。异教被定性为“religio illicita”（非法宗教）。
en: Up to that time, Rome was still more pagan than Christian. In Gaul, Spain and northern Italy, all but the urban areas remained stubbornly loyal to the old gods. Even Milan remained half pagan. But all that was about to change. In the year 392 AD, Theodosius became Emperor of both the eastern and western part of the Roman Empire; the last emperor to rule over both. In the same year he authorised the destruction of pagan temples throughout the empire. He issued a comprehensive law that prohibited the performance of any type of pagan sacrifice or worship. Paganism was proscribed as a “religio illicita”.

zh: 狄奥多西坚定不移地致力于将尼西亚基督教确立为国家唯一认可的宗教，镇压持不同信仰主张的基督徒（异端），并颁布明确的法律措施以废除异教。为了完成这项工作，他征召了大批狂热的僧侣，这些人以狂热的热情投入了破坏工作。凯瑟琳·尼克西在其著作《黑暗时代：基督教对古典世界的毁灭》中，对教会针对古代世界的宗教与文化所发动的野蛮灭绝战争，进行了犀利而真实的记述。
en: Theodosius dedicated himself steadfastly to the work of establishing a single brand of faith, Nicene Christianity, as the only accepted religion of the state, repressing dissident Christians (heretics) and enacting explicit legal measures to abolish paganism. In order to complete his work, he enlisted the services of mobs of fanatical monks, who set about the work of destruction with ferocious zeal. In her book, The Darkening Age: The Christian Destruction of the Classical World, Catherine Nixey delivers a hard-hitting and truthful account of the savage war of extermination waged by the Church against the religion and culture of the ancient world.

zh: 她以一段描述开篇：身着黑袍的狂热分子手持铁棒，摧毁了叙利亚帕尔米拉圣殿中那尊美丽的雅典娜雕像。不久前，伊斯兰国（ISIS）完成了这场破坏行为。雅典娜是智慧之神。但不仅象征这一美德的雕像遭到了残害和斩首，安提阿及其他地方的知识分子也遭到了基督徒的酷刑和斩首。尼克西写道：
en: She opens her book with a description of black-robed zealots taking iron bars to the beautiful statue of Athena in the sanctuary of Palmyra in Syria. Their vandalism was completed by ISIS not long ago. Athena was the deity of wisdom. But it was not just statues embodying this virtue that were mutilated and beheaded. Intellectuals in Antioch and elsewhere were tortured and beheaded by the Christians. Nixey writes:

zh: 达马斯基乌斯［一位希腊哲学家］的亲兄弟曾被逮捕并遭受酷刑，只为迫使他供出其他哲学家的姓名……达马斯基乌斯所在的哲学家圈子中，还有其他人曾遭受酷刑；他们被缚住手腕吊起来，直到供出其他学者的名字。几年前，一位哲学家同伴曾被活活剥皮。还有一位在法官面前遭到殴打，直到鲜血顺着他的背部流下。
en: Damascius’s [a Greek philosopher] own brother had been arrested and tortured to make him reveal the names of other philosophers… Others in Damascius’s circle of philosophers had been tortured; hung up by the wrists until they gave away the names of their fellow scholars. A fellow philosopher had, some years before, been flayed alive. Another had been beaten before a judge until the blood flowed down his back.

zh: 希帕蒂娅被害
en: THE MURDER OF HYPATIA

zh: 在哲学史上，我们很少见到女性的名字。但至少有一个值得注意的例外。亚历山大的希帕蒂娅是历史上最杰出的女性之一。
en: In the history of philosophy, we do not find the names of many women. But there is at least one notable exception to the rule. Hypatia of Alexandria was one of the most remarkable women who has ever lived.

zh: 这位非凡的女性是当时世界顶尖的数学家和天文学家。她可能是唯一一位能获得这一称号的女性。作为最后一批异教哲学家之一，她出生于公元355 年左右，尽管确切日期已不可考。然而，她于公元415 年3 月遇害，其遇害经过却众所周知。希帕蒂娅是亚历山大里亚辉煌科学学派培养出的杰出人物——这里曾是罗马帝国的知识中心，其举世闻名的图书馆中保存着古希腊罗马时期宝贵的知识遗产。
en: This extraordinary woman was the leading mathematician and astronomer in the world at the time. She is probably the only woman for whom such a claim can be made. One of the last of the pagan philosophers, she was born around the year 355 AD, though the precise date is not known. However her death occurred in March 415 AD, and the circumstances are known only too well. Hypatia was a product of the brilliant scientific school of Alexandria – the intellectual hub of the Roman Empire – where the precious heritage of the knowledge of antiquity was preserved in its world-famous library.

zh: 她的父亲同样是一位数学家和天文学家，最广为人知的是他在保存欧几里得《几何原本》方面所发挥的作用，他还著述颇丰，曾对托勒密的《天文学大成》和《便捷表》进行过评注。他毕生致力于保存希腊的数学和天文学遗产。希帕蒂娅继承了他的事业。她的哲学观点促使她选择了一生恪守贞洁的生活。她还是一位广受欢迎的教师，其关于哲学主题的讲座吸引了大批听众，并拥有众多忠实的追随者。但那是一个极其危险的时代，乌云正笼罩着希帕蒂娅及其所处的世界。她的成就引起了基督徒的怀疑。正是她的人气注定了她的命运。
en: Her father, who had also been a mathematician and astronomer, is best known for the part he played in the preservation of Euclid’s Elements, and he also wrote extensively, commenting on Ptolemy’s Almagest and Handy Tables. His life’s work was devoted to the preservation of the Greek mathematical and astronomical heritage. Hypatia continued his work. Her philosophical views led her to adopt a life of dedicated virginity. She was also a popular teacher, whose lectures on philosophical topics attracted huge audiences and a numerous following of dedicated students. But these were very dangerous times, and dark clouds were gathering over Hypatia and her world. Her successes aroused the suspicions of the Christians. It was precisely her popularity that sealed her fate.

zh: 希帕蒂娅是新柏拉图主义这一哲学流派的追随者——而这一流派实际上正是早期基督教教义的主要源泉。但亚历山大的狂热基督徒暴民对此一无所知，在他们眼中，任何哪怕稍带异教哲学气息的事物，都直接源自魔鬼之口。亚历山大与当时许多其他城市一样，是激烈宗教冲突的舞台，基督徒们在此宣泄着盲目的仇恨，时而针对犹太人，时而针对“异端”基督徒，当然，也针对所有异教徒。
en: Hypatia was an adherent to the philosophical trend known as Neoplatonism – a trend that was actually the main source of the early Christian dogma. But this fact was completely unknown to the fanatical Christian mob in Alexandria, for whom anything that smelled even remotely of pagan philosophy came straight from the mouth of the Devil. Alexandria, like many other cities at that time, was the scene of bitter religious conflicts in which Christians vented their blind hatred, now against Jews, then against ‘heretical’ Christians and, naturally, against all pagans.

zh: 亚历山大主教西奥菲勒斯摧毁塞拉皮斯神庙——即希腊-埃及神塞拉皮斯的庙宇——便是早期的预警。这一事件标志着伟大的亚历山大图书馆的最终覆灭，因为塞拉皮斯神庙似乎收藏了该图书馆的部分书籍。然而，西奥菲勒斯与希帕蒂娅的仰慕者兼学生西内西乌斯关系友好，因此她本人并未受到这一事态的影响，仍被允许不受阻碍地继续她的学术事业。但她已随时面临死亡。她的生命悬于一线，随时都可能断裂。
en: An early warning was the razing of the Serapeum, the temple of the Greco-Egyptian god Seraphis by Alexandria’s bishop Theophilus. This event marked the final end of the great Library of Alexandria, since the Serapeum seems to have contained some of the Library’s books. Theophilus, however, was friendly with Synesius, an admirer and pupil of Hypatia, so she was not herself affected by this development and was permitted to pursue her endeavours unimpeded. But she was living on borrowed time. Her life was hanging by a slender thread, which could break at any moment.

zh: 这种脆弱的平衡因西奥菲勒斯的去世以及凶残的狂热分子西里尔继任亚历山大主教而突然被打破。原本不安定的宽容氛围随之消散，不久之后，希帕蒂娅便成为了一起特别残暴的谋杀案的受害者。
en: This fragile equilibrium was suddenly destroyed by the death of Theophilus and the accession of Cyril, a vicious bigot, to the bishopric of Alexandria. The uneasy climate of tolerance lapsed and, shortly afterward, Hypatia became the victim of a particularly brutal murder.

zh: 她被一群被盲目仇恨和嗜血狂热所煽动的基督徒暴徒以难以言喻的残忍手段残杀。索拉亚·菲尔德·菲奥里奥如此描述当时的情景：
en: She was butchered with indescribable cruelty by a Christian mob, fired up by blind hatred and blood lust. Soraya Field Fiorio describes the scene:

zh: 公元415 年早春的一天，在亚历山大城——这个日渐衰落的罗马帝国的文化中心——异教哲学家希帕蒂娅被一群基督教男子杀害。这些人，即“帕拉巴拉尼”，是一支由僧侣组成的志愿民兵，充当大主教的打手。他们被征召的初衷是照料死者和垂死之人，但更常见的是他们恐吓敌对的基督教派，并夷平异教神庙。在亚历山大主教西里尔的怂恿下，他们早已摧毁了亚历山大图书馆的残骸。帕拉巴拉尼摧毁异教神庙，袭击犹太人聚居区，并通过残害雕像、熔化取金的方式，玷污了他们视为恶魔附体的古代艺术杰作。如今，他们将目光投向了这座城市备受爱戴的数学与哲学教师——她的社会地位与亚历山大最显赫的人物并驾齐驱。这些人对她的哲学一无所知，却称她为女巫。当这位年迈的教师驾着马车穿行于城市时，他们将她从车上拽下，拖拽至一座神庙。她被剥得一丝不挂，皮肤被参差锋利的牡蛎壳碎片剥下，四肢被从躯干上扯下，在街头游街示众。她的遗体被焚烧，这简直是对异教祭祀的嘲弄。希帕蒂娅之死标志着异教的终结与基督教的胜利，也是新宗教与古老世界之间长达百年恩怨的最终篇章。
en: One early spring day during the year 415 in the city of Alexandria – the intellectual heart of the waning Roman Empire – the pagan philosopher Hypatia was murdered by a mob of Christian men. These men, the parabalani, were a volunteer militia of monks serving as henchmen to the archbishop. Their conscripted purpose was to aid the dead and dying but they could be more readily found terrorising opposing Christian groups and levelling pagan temples. At the urging of Cyril, bishop of Alexandria, they had already destroyed the remains of the Library of Alexandria. The parabalani razed pagan temples, attacked the Jewish quarters, and defiled masterpieces of ancient art they considered demonic by mutilating statues and melting them down for gold. They now set their gaze on the city’s beloved teacher of mathematics and philosophy, whose social ranking was on par with Alexandria’s most important men. Understanding nothing of her philosophy, they called her a witch. They pulled the elderly teacher from her chariot as she rode through the city and dragged her to a temple. She was stripped naked, her skin flayed with jagged pieces of oyster shells, her limbs pulled from her body and paraded through the streets. Her remains were burned in a mockery of pagan sacrifice. Hypatia’s death marked the end of paganism and the triumph of Christianity, the final act of a one-hundred-year-old feud waged by the new religion against the ancient world.

zh: 就这样，古希腊罗马时代最后一位杰出的哲学家逝去了。随着她的离世，一个充满光明与文化的世界也随之消逝。欧洲陷入了长达千年的黑暗、无知与迷信之中。用威廉·曼彻斯特的话来说，那是一个仅靠火焰照亮的世界。
en: Thus perished the last notable philosopher of antiquity. With her an entire world of light and culture passed away. Europe was plunged into a world of darkness, ignorance and superstition that lasted a thousand years. To quote the words of William Manchester, it was a world lit only by fire.
